article.contentMarkdown:
# Raksha Bandhan Video Maker With Photo and Music: MP4 or Link?

A Raksha Bandhan video maker with photo and music does one of two genuinely different jobs, and most tools only admit to one of them. An MP4 editor hands you a file you can post anywhere. SubhSandesh does not: it publishes a moving, animated page behind a private link, no MP4 comes out of it, and the rakhi template carries no audio track today. Those pages have collected 32,683 recorded views at an average of 12.0 views each, so links do get opened — in a browser, by a person who tapped, not as a file sitting in someone's gallery. This page compares the two formats on the four things that actually decide which one you want: whether the music is legally yours to post, whether it plays on the first tap, whether you can tell your brother opened it, and whether it works with no signal at all.

## What a "Raksha Bandhan video maker with photo and music" actually produces

It produces one of three things: an MP4 file, a hosted video page, or an animated web page. Only the first is a file you own and can forward; the others are links needing a browser and a live connection.

That distinction matters more than any feature list. An MP4 is portable and silent about its audience; a page is fragile without a network but can count opens.

Slideshow apps and browser editors sit in the first camp. SubhSandesh sits in the third — one rakhi template among the 13 page types it has published so far — and "video maker" is not an honest description of it.

## The five constraints that decide which format you should use

Every constraint below is a real limit, not a preference. Each names what it is, who it hits, the number behind it, and what to do.

### 1. Audio rights on anything public

A film song in a public post is the constraint people discover last. On YouTube, a Content ID match can block, monetise or track your upload, and [YouTube's own documentation on Content ID claims](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/6013276?hl=en) states that a claimed Short between one and three minutes long **will be blocked regardless of which policy the rights holder chose** — and since 15 October 2024 every new vertical video of that length is categorised as a Short.

So a 90-second vertical rakhi video with a Bollywood track is the single most likely thing to disappear. Private sharing is a different question in Indian law; for a public reel, a licensed in-app track is the safe move.

The file you upload is also not the file that plays. YouTube's [recommended upload encoding settings](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/1722171?hl=en) ask for an MP4 container, H.264 video and 48 kHz AAC-LC audio — a fair measure of how little control you keep once a platform has your track.

### 2. When a song is actually free to use

Old songs are the loophole nobody in this category mentions. The Government of India's [Copyright Office handbook](https://copyright.gov.in/documents/handbook.html) states the general term of copyright is 60 years, and that for sound recordings, cinematograph films and photographs the 60-year period runs from the date of publication rather than the author's death.

That means a recording published up to 1965 is outside its term in 2026, while a 2019 film song has another 53 years to run. If you want music with no claim risk at all, an old recording or a royalty-free track is the only reliable answer.

### 3. Whether the music plays on the first tap

A page that carries music cannot decide to play it. [Chrome's autoplay policy](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/autoplay), in force since Chrome 66, allows muted autoplay always but permits sound only after the user has interacted with the domain, or on desktop once a Media Engagement Index threshold is crossed — and the MEI route is explicitly desktop-only.

Since 51.9% of shared SubhSandesh pages are opened on a phone, over half of all recipients land where sound needs a deliberate tap. An MP4 in a chat thread has the same problem in reverse: it plays muted in the preview until tapped.

### 4. Whether you can tell it was opened

An MP4 forwarded on WhatsApp reports nothing back. Once delivered, you cannot distinguish a brother who watched it four times from one who never opened the chat.

A link can be counted, which is the only reason the 32,683 recorded views figure exists at all. If knowing matters to you, that asymmetry is the strongest single argument for a link.

### 5. Whether it survives with no signal

A file works on a plane and in a village with one bar; a page does not. This is where SubhSandesh straightforwardly loses, and it is not a small case in India. If your brother's connection is unreliable, or he keeps things in his gallery for years, send a file and stop reading comparisons.

## MP4 versus a shareable page, on real values

Here is the same job costed both ways. The right-hand column is SubhSandesh's own measured data, which no video app can print.

| What you care about | MP4 from a slideshow app | Animated page on SubhSandesh |
|---|---|---|
| Music | Your own track, baked into the file | None on the rakhi template today |
| Plays without a tap | Muted preview, then a tap | Muted until a tap, on all mobile |
| Works with no signal | Yes, once downloaded | No |
| Opens you can see | Zero | 32,683 views, 12.0 per page average |
| Private by default | No, forwardable to anyone | Optional password, used by 44.3% |

The takeaway is narrow: an MP4 wins on portability and offline life, a page wins on privacy and on knowing who opened it.

## Which song actually makes him remember something

The music choice is not a taste question — it is a retrieval question, and there is real evidence on it. In a study of 233 adults published in PLOS One on 20 August 2025, [Nawaz and Omigie found](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0329072) that quieter, more acoustic songs were associated with memories rated as more vivid, more unique and more personally important, while high-energy songs were **less likely to evoke a memory at all** (p = 0.003) and took measurably longer to retrieve when they did.

That is the opposite of what the category assumes: the loud festival track at the top of every rakhi template list is, on this evidence, the weaker memory cue.

Familiarity is the mechanism, which is why a generated festive loop is a weaker choice than the song you both actually know. In [a 2025 PLOS One study of 88 viewers](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0326498), Fišer and colleagues scored AI-generated soundtracks as significantly less familiar than human-composed music (3.00 against 3.31 on a five-point scale, p < 0.001) and recorded wider pupil dilation while people listened to them.

The authors read that dilation as effort spent decoding the sound. So pick the track from the year you both remember, then choose the photographs that agree with its mood — not whatever the app generated for the occasion.

## When an MP4 editor is the right choice and SubhSandesh is the wrong one

Use a real MP4 editor in four cases. First, if the thing is going on a public Instagram Reel, a WhatsApp Status or a YouTube Short — a link in a Status is a dead end, and a page cannot be a Reel.

Second, if your brother's phone or connection is unreliable, because a file plays and a page does not. Third, if he keeps things: a page can be deleted or unpublished, a downloaded file cannot.

Fourth, and most importantly, **if music is the point**, because the SubhSandesh rakhi template ships with no audio at all today.

That last one is worth being blunt about. Several other templates on the platform do carry a looping background track — the [romantic "I love you" page](https://subhsandesh.in/love-gf) is one, and at 913 pages created it is also the most-made template on the site. The rakhi page is not one of them.

If you searched for "video maker with photo and music" and the music is non-negotiable, SubhSandesh answers only two-thirds of your query. An MP4 app answers all three.

## What the SubhSandesh rakhi page does instead, in about ten minutes

What it gives you is a sequence rather than a file: animated tilak, aarti and rakhi-tying scenes, a hero photo of the two of you, and a memories reel that takes up to 12 photos, each with its own caption and year.

You also get six lines of greeting text, an eight-row "what you did for me" ledger, and a space for his written promise back. The [Raksha Bandhan page for a brother](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-rakshabandhan-to-brother) is the only rakhi template on the site, so there is no choosing to do.

Three measured behaviours are worth knowing before you start. 44.3% of creators password-protect the page before sharing it, which is the one feature no MP4 has.

99.4% of started pages actually get published and shared, so the drop-off people expect from a builder is not showing up. And the median gap between a page's first save and its last edit is 6.9 hours, sampled across 913 "I love you" pages.

That last number is the practical one: people write, leave, and come back before sending. Start the night before rather than on the morning of.

Across 2,718 pages created since 12 March 2026 in 13 page types the pattern holds: these are not one-shot artefacts, they get revised. If that sounds like your process, [browse the template gallery](https://subhsandesh.in/templates) and start early. If you want a file you can forward tonight with a song under it, an MP4 app is the correct tool.

## Sources

- Nawaz, S. and Omigie, D., "Qualities of music-evoked autobiographical memories are associated with auditory features of the memory-evoking music", *PLOS One* 20(8): e0329072 — published 20 August 2025. [Read it](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0329072)
- Fišer, N., Martín-Pascual, M.Á. and Andreu-Sánchez, C., "Emotional impact of AI-generated vs. human-composed music in audiovisual media", *PLOS One* 20(6): e0326498 — published 25 June 2025. [Read it](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0326498)
- "Learn about Content ID claims", [YouTube Help](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/6013276?hl=en) — no publication date given.
- "Recommended upload encoding settings", [YouTube Help](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/1722171?hl=en) — no publication date given.
- "Autoplay policy in Chrome", [Chrome for Developers](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/autoplay) — last updated 13 September 2017.
- "A Hand Book of Copyright Law", [Copyright Office, Government of India](https://copyright.gov.in/documents/handbook.html) — no publication date given.
- First-party product data from SubhSandesh's own database, measured 18 August 2026.

auditReport.honestAssessment: It is the only page for this query that states its own product cannot do the thing the query asks for — no MP4 export, no audio on the rakhi template — and it is the only one carrying verified numbers on either side of the choice: YouTube's rule that a claimed 1-3 minute vertical video is blocked regardless of policy, India's 60-years-from-publication term for sound recordings, Chrome's desktop-only autoplay exception, and 32,683 first-party recorded views.
